styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Red Rocks, foothills trails and mountain views.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Green chile, food halls and brewery taps.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, street art and a gold-rush past.

stays.why: Historic core by Union Station. Walk to Coors Field, the river and most of downtown. Best first-timer base.
Central, close to the 16th Street Mall and light rail. Quieter at weekends when offices empty.
Cheaper, leafy streets near museums and Cheesman Park. Good cafés and nightlife on nearby Colfax.
Mural-covered warehouse district with breweries and food halls. Lively, a short ride from downtown.

food: Try a green chile dish: smothered burritos and breakfast burritos are a local staple. Ask about heat level.
Denver has many breweries and taprooms. RiNo and LoDo are the easiest clusters to walk between.
Food halls are handy for groups: look for one downtown or in RiNo and check current opening hours.
Rocky Mountain oysters and bison appear on menus; try them if you are curious.
High altitude can affect you: drink water, go easy on alcohol on day one, and eat a proper meal before a big hike.
more_time: Add a day in the mountains: Boulder or Golden are short drives or bus rides from Denver; check current schedules.
Swap a city afternoon for Red Rocks Park and Amphitheatre; check whether a show or event is on.
Museum lovers can spend a half day at the Denver Art Museum or the Denver Museum of Nature & Science.

recommend.why: Two nights covers downtown, a museum and a foothills or Red Rocks outing; add a night if you want a full mountain day.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 5°C and lows around -10°C. Pack layers and watch for snow and ice.
February: still cold, similar to January. A good month for museums and indoor sights.
March: warming to highs near 11°C but lows still below freezing. Snow is possible.
April: mild days near 16°C, cold nights near 0°C. Rain and snow showers are common.
May: pleasant highs near 20°C. Wettest month by rain days, so carry a light rain jacket.
June: warm and mostly dry, highs near 28°C. Strong sun at altitude; use sunscreen.
July: hottest month, highs near 31°C. Afternoon thunderstorms are common; plan hikes for the morning.
August: hot like July, highs near 30°C. Stay hydrated and watch afternoon storms.
September: warm days near 28°C and fewer rain days. A great month for trails and patios.
October: cooler, highs near 19°C and lows near 3°C. Crisp days; pack a warm layer.
November: chilly, highs near 11°C with freezing nights. Snow becomes more likely.
December: cold, highs near 7°C and lows around -7°C. Dress warm for downtown evenings.

climate_guide.summary: High-altitude, semi-arid climate: sunny much of the year, cold winters, warm summers and quick afternoon storms in summer.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Warm, mostly dry days with highs around 28–31°C. Ideal for trails and outdoor sights.

items.title: Winter is cold (December to February)
items.text: Highs near 5–7°C and lows around -10°C. Snow and ice are possible; bring a warm coat and boots.

items.title: Summer afternoon storms
items.text: July and August often bring afternoon thunderstorms. Hike early and be off exposed ridges by midday.

items.title: Wettest in spring
items.text: May has the most rain days (about 13). Carry a light rain jacket in spring.

items.title: High altitude
items.text: Denver sits about a mile high. Take it easy on day one, drink water and use sunscreen.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers year-round, a warm jacket for winter, sun protection in summer and sturdy shoes for trails.

transit.best: Walk downtown and use RTD light rail or buses; use ride apps for late nights and spots outside the core.

modes.text: RTD light rail and commuter rail link downtown, suburbs and the airport. Check fares and schedules on the day.
RTD buses cost $2.75 cash with a 3-hour transfer; day passes about $5.50.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Lyft both work well in Denver.
A car is handy outside downtown; toll roads are cashless, so check rental billing.
Downtown is walkable; bikes and scooters are common in summer.
No ferry service; the city is landlocked.
